string.text: Draw expanding rings on screen at the position of any sound source, even through walls.
Show rings for the player's own footsteps and gunshots. Off by default - you always feel your own sounds.
World polling radius (footsteps, physics, anomalies). In the distance mode (audibility off) - the single show limit.
How long one expanding wave lives before fading out.
Minimum pause between waves from the same sound source. Smaller = more waves, more clutter.
Size of the ring for a close sound source (in HUD virtual pixels).
At this distance a ring has full size. Farther sources get smaller rings.
How small the ring can get for the farthest sounds, percent of full size (5-50).
How many expanding rings are drawn for one sound (1-3, sonar style).
Overall opacity of the rings, percent (20-100).
White rings: talking, shouts, screams, pain cries.
Yellow rings: anyone walking or running nearby, even behind walls.
Purple rings: mutant sounds - steps, growls, attacks.
Turquoise rings: idle hum of anomalies and activation hiss (bolt, approach, entry).
Blue rings: pushed barrels and boxes, knife hits, dropped items, grenades, falling bodies.
How often each nearby anomaly pulses while idling (its hum plays periodically). Real anomalies hum every few seconds.
Watch physical objects near the player: a pushed or knocked barrel, a sliding box, a thrown grenade all produce rings. Disable if it causes clutter.
How far an object must move to count as "makes sound". Lower = more sensitive (more rings). Default 12 cm.
Since v2.7 every caught sound is shown (no loudness gate), so this only affects world polling: on - per-category range cap, off - the single detection radius. Keep it on.

The red ring is placed by fact: every 0.2 s the ammo counter of each stalker within 250 m is read - if it drops, a shot happened. Works on any build, with any weapon pack, and for a lone shooter with no other NPCs nearby. Also: when you get hit, a ring is placed on the attacker immediately. Suppressors are respected: silenced shots show at a shorter range.

Vignette mask: in the very center of the screen (crosshair area) rings fade to almost nothing - you look there with your own eyes and see what happens (shooting, enemies). Toward the screen edges rings return to full brightness, so nothing gets lost.
How much of the usual brightness remains in the very center. 10 = about one tenth of the normal rings.
How far from the screen center the dim zone extends, percent of the way from center to screen edge. Rings inside it keep the "Center brightness".
Distance from the center where rings reach full brightness again, percent of the way to the screen edge. 100 = at the edges. Between the dim zone and this radius brightness grows smoothly.

The mod checks line of sight to each sound source (a level raycast, done sparingly and cached). A source you see directly becomes translucent so it does not cover the enemy; a source behind a wall gets a blurred halo at the "Behind-wall brightness" - key information for hard-of-hearing players: everyone else hears the enemy behind the wall, you have to SEE him. Closed doors are not seen by the ray - such sources show as visible.
Brightness of rings for sources you see directly (no wall between you and them). 40 = 60% transparent - a hint, not a cover. Sources behind walls are configured separately - "Behind-wall brightness".

Brightness of rings for sources hidden by a wall. The key setting for hard-of-hearing players: everyone else hears the enemy behind the wall - you have to SEE him. Default 70 - noticeably brighter than visible sources (40). 100 = like a normal ring in the open.

Sources behind walls draw with a soft blurred ring texture (muddy halo) - a visual hint that the sound comes from behind an obstacle. Blurring does not reduce brightness: the soft texture peak matches the normal ring (v2.8.1).
How much wider the blurred halo of a wall-blocked source is, percent of the normal ring size (100 = same size).

If enabled, the center vignette also dims sources behind walls (v2.8 behavior). Off by default: you are staring at the wall with the enemy behind it - the ring must be bright right there, not hidden by the vignette.

Full pipeline trace to the game log (appdata\logs\xray_*.log): HEAR/SHOT/RELOAD - sound caught by a channel; GATE - queue rejected it and why (threshold, distance, category, anti-spam); QUEUE - event accepted; RENDER - ring shown or why not; INIT - which callbacks registered on this build. Look for lines prefixed [sound_vision]. Turn off after diagnosing.

Every new sound type is written to the game log as [sound_vision][TYPES] s_type '...' -> category. Add those strings to sound_vision_overrides.script to recolor any sounds of your modpack. Turn off after tuning.
